title: DARPA TTO Office-Wide BAA HR001125S0011
summary: The TTO office-wide BAA frames research around designing and building advanced platforms, buying and adapting capability quickly, surging and sustaining systems, long-range effects, and disruptive innovation. The common dependency is the ability to move complex hardware from design into operationally sustainable systems.
key_findings: TTO links platform design, rapid acquisition, production, adaptation, and sustainment.
Autonomy, propulsion, long-range effects, and complex systems must be integrated with build and support capacity.
Surge and sustainment are treated as capability requirements rather than post-deployment logistics.
why_it_matters: It makes production speed, adaptability, and sustainment part of the technology thesis for advanced platforms.
ftfn_relevance: Connects aviation, mobility, space, autonomy, and manufacturing to operational logistics.
Supports tracking whether prototypes have credible production and support pathways.
evidence_limits: The archived BAA page is no longer available from DARPA; the local capture is the current TTO office page and the official notice link remains on SAM.gov.
The BAA identifies interest areas, not awards, prototypes, procurement, or fielded capacity.
